description: We’re a group interested in space, science and creative problem-solving. We enjoy researching, developing ideas and turning them into creative projects. We’re looking for curious and motivated teammates who are interested in space, storytelling, design or communication. No advanced skills are required, beginners are welcome! Join our group if you want to have fun and learn!
summary:
We developed an interactive website that explores the forgotten traces of human space exploration on the Moon and Mars. Through dedicated sections, interactive maps and visual storytelling, users can discover abandoned spacecraft, rovers, landers and historic mission sites, learning about the missions behind them.

Our project addresses the Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge by making the locations and historical significance of the objects left behind on other worlds easier to explore and understand. Instead of viewing these objects as forgotten equipment, we present them as valuable records of scientific progress and human exploration.

This matters because every space mission leaves behind a part of humanity’s history. Preserving and sharing these traces helps future generations understand how far we have come, appreciate past achievements and recognize the legacy of space exploration as humanity continues to explore the universe.
details:
1. What Does Our Project Do and How Does It Work?
BeyondGravity is an interactive website that explores the objects humans have left behind in space, focusing on the Moon and Mars. Users can follow a storyline, explore interactive maps, watch videos and read explanations about different objects. By clicking on individual objects, they can discover their history, purpose and the stories behind them. We also created an interactive timeline that connects objects with important moments in space exploration.
2. What Are the Benefits and Intended Impact?
Our goal is to make the history of space exploration more accessible, interesting and understandable. Instead of just reading facts, users can actively explore and discover things themselves. We want to raise awareness of the historical and scientific value of these objects and show why they should not simply be forgotten.
3. What Tools and Technologies Did We Use?
We used Claude and Gemini to support us with ideas and development, GitHub and Google Sites to build and manage our website and our laptops to develop the project.
4. How Is Our Project Creative?
We combined storytelling, interactive maps, videos and an interactive timeline to create a more engaging learning experience. Users are not just presented with information but can explore different objects themselves, follow their stories and discover the history behind them.
5. What Factors Did Our Team Consider?
We focused on making the website easy to navigate and the information understandable and interesting. We wanted to create something that would appeal to people even if they have little knowledge about space exploration, while still providing meaningful information about the objects left behind.
